bib.title: EAGLE-2: Faster Inference of Language Models with Dynamic Draft Trees

question: Can the static draft tree of EAGLE be replaced by a context-aware dynamic draft tree that raises accepted tokens per cycle without extra training or changing the output distribution?
hypothesis: Draft-token acceptance depends on context as well as position, and the draft model's confidence approximates acceptance rate well enough to shape the tree.
contributions: Observe that acceptance rate is context-dependent and that EAGLE's draft model is well-calibrated
Propose EAGLE-2: expansion by global value and reranking to build a dynamic draft tree, no extra training, lossless
Evaluate on three LLM series and six tasks, 3.05x-4.26x speedup, 20%-40% faster than EAGLE-1

method.summary: EAGLE-2 keeps EAGLE's draft model and verification unchanged. It grows the draft tree layer by layer, expanding the top-k nodes by value (product of draft confidences along the path), then reranks all nodes, keeps the top m, flattens them and verifies with a tree attention mask.

limits: No hardware (GPU type, batch size) is stated; speedups are hardware-dependent and only batch-style single-request use is implied.
Tree-size settings (60/50/48 tokens, depth 6, k=10) are given without a tuning study or sensitivity analysis.
No variance, seeds or repeated runs reported.
Lower gains on summarization and QA, attributed by the authors to SFT-only draft-model training data.
Medusa, Hydra and others are not compared at temperature 1 because they relax acceptance conditions.

terms.definition: The average number of tokens generated per drafting-verification cycle, which corresponds to the number of tokens accepted from the draft.
Product of the draft confidence scores along the path from root to a node, approximating its global acceptance rate.
